text.p: Germany's Vereinsbank said on Friday it had upgraded its recommendation on luxury car maker Porsche to "above average" from "market neutral" and sharply raised its earnings per share estimates.
"The figures for the 1995/96 business year were considerably above our expectations," said Vereinsbank analyst Georg Stuerzer in a research note to clients.

Vereinsbank said it had raised its earnings per share estimate for 1995/96 to 28 marks ($18.63) from 11 marks and to 56.5 marks from 24.5 marks for 1996/97. It said it saw 73 marks earnings per share achievable in 1997/98.
"With the success of the Boxter (Porsche's new model) and the unchanged high demand for the 911 model, Porsche will push the boundaries of its capacity next year," Vereinsbank said.

On November 8, Porsche reported its highest net profit in six years, gaining 48 million marks for the 1995/96 business year to the end of July. The company also said it would be able to pay out a dividend, 2.50 marks, for the first time since 1991/92.
The share has risen sharply since the firm published results, gaining over 20 percent since November 13.
On Thursday Porsche shares rose 90 marks, or over eight percent, to 1,210 marks. Earlier in the day it touched a new year high of 1,260 marks. ($ = 1.502 German Marks)
